items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: Well, I received a letter from Leonard Feather, and wanting to know if I would be interested in coming to London to arrange for the BBC dance orchestra,

ctx.x: Right. Then you -- at the end of these tours, you always went back to London and you made a number of recording sessions there with Vocalion I think, a new label, and Leonard Feather, I think, was involved in some of those.
Well, I think Leonard was involved in all of them.

items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Oh yeah, everything I think that I did, he produced, everything I did there.

ctx.x: Eventually you went to England, and that, I believe came about through your friend, long-term friend, Leonard Feather.

That’s right. We had never met, and I got a cable from Leonard, asking me if I would be interested in coming to London [England] to work for the BBC [British Broadcasting Company] as an arranger. That was very interesting to me. I corresponded with him and answered, of course, in the affirmative, and he worked out a deal with the BBC for me to come there. I think I went there in March of maybe 1936.
